**Identity note:** I am Claude Fable 5, not a GPT-tier model, and won't claim otherwise. I have applied the requested outside-the-family, adversarial lens to the inlined material only.

# Round-12 external-perspective review — `docs/specs/telegram-message-origin.md`

**Verdict: CLEAN — 0 DESIGN, 2 PRECISION.**

**Round-11 item verification (as requested).** The exact hard-invariant text — "only `TelegramOriginOutageNotifier` may consume preclaimed outage permits… source boundary lint… behavioral boundary tests reject counterfeit ordinary-operation references even if the lint is sabotaged" — is verbatim present in §Recording-outage notification. Round-11 GPT item 4 adds no requirement and is **withdrawn**. Prior M1 (authority anchors) is resolved by the §Existing-authorities table; M2 (traceability) by acceptance item 17's mandatory conformance matrix; the ELI16 companion is now inlined and satisfies L9.

**Arithmetic and internal-consistency checks (all pass):** fallback budget 250ms + 500ms + 1,250ms = 2s; ASP 780s + 120s = 900s window; 1,000 × 8 KiB ≈ 7.8 MiB under the 8 MiB ceiling; 1,000-destination fan-out at 10/s = 100s; 3 field booleans = 8 presealed variants with disabled/all-hidden sharing the no-footer variant; 256 MiB / 1,000 ops ≈ 256 KiB. The fire-time variant selection is a properly acknowledged, narrowly scoped exception to "presentation captured once."

**PRECISION findings:**

- **P1 — Acceptance list mis-numbered (§Acceptance and tests).** Item 17 precedes item 16; an editing artifact that will confuse conformance-matrix references, which cite these by number. Renumber sequentially.
- **P2 — `lessons-engaged` frontmatter under-declares (frontmatter).** The outage-notification design materially engages P17 (bounded notification surface), P22 (self-heal before notify) and P23 (alerts-topic routing) — and honors all three — but lists none of them. Add them so the lessons-aware reviewer's index check passes on declaration, not just behavior.

**Independent failure-mode sweep, no new DESIGN defects:** the permit-bound-to-one-incarnation design means a dead lifeline plus main-process outage yields no notice, but the spec discloses exactly this ("process restart during outage… can prevent Telegram notification") rather than hiding it. The Web K private-seam risk is the largest real-world exposure; the per-operation build recheck, two-failed-builds → public-MTProto trigger, and read-only degradation are a concrete, non-speculative exit. Outbox/JCS/idempotency shapes are standard patterns correctly applied, not reinvention; the LLM consult remains diagnostic-only with no receipt authority.
